clinicalSources.title: NHS children’s health: Sleepwalking, nightmares and night terrors

teaching.question: Which timing and recall pattern helps distinguish a night terror from a nightmare?
teaching.answer: A night terror typically occurs early in deep non-REM sleep and leaves little recall. A nightmare occurs in REM, often later, with full waking and remembered dream content.

title: Night terror or nightmare?
caption: Night terrors typically arise early from deep non-REM sleep with little recall. Nightmares occur in REM sleep, often later, and the child can wake and recall the dream.
alt: A night ribbon places night terrors near sleep onset and nightmares nearer morning, with contrasting blank and remembered dream icons.

review.notes: Night terror is positioned early relative to sleep onset and explicitly labelled deep non-REM with little/no recall. Nightmare is later relative to morning and labelled REM with remembered star postcard. No arrow implies one disorder causes the other. Timing qualifier excludes fixed schedule; no invented sleep recording.
